newsitem.title: USA: WPL Holdings says regulators advance merger.
newsitem.headline: WPL Holdings says regulators advance merger.

text.p: An administrative law judge has recommended that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approve a proposed Interstate Energy Corp merger involving WPL Holdings Inc, IES Industries Inc and Interstate Power Co.
The proposed order will go to the FERC in early August, with a final decision expected in September or October, WPL Holdings said in a news release disclosing the judge's recommendation.

In a proposed order to the FERC, Presiding Administrative Law Judge Bruce Birchman said the conditions agreed to by the IEC merger partners and the FERC staff eliminated concerns about market power as a result of the merger.

"The proposed approval order states that there is no basis for denying the IEC merger," said Erroll Davis Jr., president and chief executive officer of WPL Holdings. "Under conditions that IEC has already accepted, there will be absolutely no market power or anti-competition concerns as a result of the merger."

Earlier this year, the IEC partners and the FERC staff reached an agreement on how to address potential market-power concerns. As part of the agreement, IEC has contracted to purchase transmission capacity to interconnect the three utility systems. A portion of that capacity will be made available for purchase by other utilities on a first-come, first-served basis, under terms and conditions established by the FERC.

IEC agreed that it would not seek to build transmission lines to directly interconnect the three utility systems until it had first constructed at least 400 megawatts of additional simultaneous transmission import capability into Wisconsin. To accomplish this, IEC has proposed eight different transmission projects.
